---
title: "How to read this course"
---

Every chapter is written in three layers, and you choose how deep to
go. Nothing in a deeper layer is required to follow the layer above it.

## The three layers

**Intuition first.** Each chapter opens with a few paragraphs of plain
prose — no equations, no code. Read only these openings and the
takeaway lists and you will still get the whole argument: why a DCF has
two free numbers, why persistent consumption risk carries a price, and
why value out-earns growth. Prerequisite: finance at the level of
knowing what a dividend, a return, and a price–earnings ratio are.

**Derivations on demand.** The mathematics lives in collapsible
callouts marked "Derivation". They are closed by default; open them
when you want to see where an equation comes from rather than take it
on faith. Prerequisite: comfort with expectations, logs, and the idea
of a stochastic discount factor — first-year asset pricing.

**Code you can run.** Every number on this site is printed at build
time by the code cell directly above it. Cells are folded where the
code is plumbing and open where the code *is* the point. Prerequisite:
enough Python to read a short script.

## What each part does

- **Part I — The Puzzle.** The DCF's two free numbers, and the value
  premium as it appears in 74 years of data.
- **Part II — The Toolkit.** The Euler equation, Epstein–Zin
  preferences, and the long-run risks endowment — the three pieces any
  general-equilibrium valuation needs.
- **Part III — Solving the Model.** Two solution methods: a log-linear
  approximation you can read economics off, and a quadrature grid that
  checks it.
- **Part IV — Confronting the Data.** Calibrating cash flows without
  touching returns, testing the market claim, and pricing the value
  premium.
- **Part V — Your Turn.** Price your own claim with the same recipe,
  then read where the model misses and how far to trust it.

## How to run the code

Clone and install with `uv`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tlorans/kiku-value-premium-replication.git
cd kiku-value-premium-replication
uv pip install -e ".[fast,data]"
```

Or take a single chapter: every chapter page offers a notebook download
under **Other Formats** (top of the page). The notebooks fetch the data
files they need if you run them outside the repository, so the only
setup is the package itself:

```bash
pip install "lrrcs[fast] @ git+https://github.com/tlorans/kiku-value-premium-replication.git"
```

Details, extras, and the optional WRDS credentials are in
[Installation](reference/installation.qmd).

## The numbers policy

No number in the prose is typed in by hand. Every figure, table, and
in-text statistic is printed by the code cell above it when the site is
built; the prose is written to match the output, never the other way
around. Numbers that come from Kiku's paper rather than from this
code are always attributed as such ("Table IX reports…"). If a cell's
output and the surrounding prose ever disagree, the cell is right and
the prose is a bug — please report it.
